notes: §1985:XIII.3.6.4 GR1: "literal-1 is automatically placed in the first two character positions of each report writer logical record", and GR2 keeps those positions out of the print line and in the record size. BindCodeClause/Screen85CodeLiteral bind the two-character literal at 85 (refusing other lengths and identifiers), EmitReportConstruction passes it to ReportWriter.SetCode, and PresentLine composes every record as _code + line.Compose(), so COLUMN 1 lands in record position 3. Probed at 85 with two reports in one file (CODE "AB" and "CD") through RH, PH, details, CF, PF and a page advance: every record written begins with its own report's code (ABRA-RH, CDRB-DT, AB  CF-A for COLUMN 3) and a 20-character line fills RECORD CONTAINS 22; blank spacing lines carry no record (record structure implementor-defined, §1985:XIII.3.2.4 GR2). Refusals: CODE on one report only COBOL2713 (SR2), "A", "ABC", "", 12, SPACES and an identifier COBOL2713, CODE twice COBOL2423. Lead for the format row: CODE IS "AB" is accepted at 85, but the printed §1985:XIII.3.6.2 (page 596 rendered) is CODE literal-1 with no IS; BindCodeClause's comment misquotes it as CODE IS literal-1. Witness: a report record read back as a plain file starts with AB.

next.reason: 1985: "literal-1 is automatically placed in the first two character positions of each report writer logical record"; 2023: "literal-1 or identifier-1 is automatically placed in the first characters of each logical record written to the report file". 2023 drops the fixed two-character position (its SR-13.18.12.3-1 sets no length) and adds identifier-1 as an alternative source of the code.
